newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks hold gains to noon, light trade.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks hold gains to noon, light trade.

text.p: SPI Futures 2441 +3 US 30yr cl 7.05 -0.02
10yrbond futs 92.130 -0.035 Gold NY 341.35 Lon fix 342.10
*Stocks go to midsession little changed from opening, trade light, gold explorers feature. Volume 151.60 million, value A$213.85 million, 805 stocks traded, 308 steady, 315 up, 182 down.

The Australian share market went to the midsession firmer but little changed from its opening levels on Monday with the continuing rally on Wall Street providing further support to optimistic local traders.
By 12.05 p.m. (0205 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 5.5 points at 2,447.9. June share price index futures were up three points at 2,441, a 6.9 point discount to the index.

Apart from a brief foray to the day's highs of 2,454.5, a mixed market spent most of the morning treading water with only National Australia Bank notable among the leaders as traders bought in ahead of the big bank's first half results.
"It went for a bit of a run mid-morning but otherwise it's been content to stay where it is," said a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage.
Others agreed, saying while the market's mood was positive, trade had been patchy rather than all one-way traffic.
"It's nothing startling but it's doing okay. There is no real pattern in the market," said one broker.

National Australia Bank jumped over 1.6 percent to A$16.78 as traders anticipated a strong first half profit result after the bank suspended its share buyback scheme ahead of the results' release scheduled for May 15.
Impressive drilling results put a healthy shine on several gold explorers.
Carpenter Pacific Resources NL and Ramsgate Resources NL jumped as traders digested Friday's results from the Mt Kare project in Papua New Guinea.
By midday, Carpenter shares were 20 percent higher at 45.5 cents on heavy turnover of 10.8 million shares, while Ramsgate shares up 21 percent at 11.5 cents on turnover of 16 million.
Arcadia Minerals NL and Sipa Resources NL also climbed high after well-received drilling results from their Mt Olympus gold prospect in Western Australia.
Arcadia climbed 25 percent to 99 cents, albeit on thin trade, while Sipa also jumped 17 percent to 56 cents.

Fellow explorer Golden Valley Mines NL jumped over 50 percent to 65 cents amid speculation it was close to announcing a new deal on a gold project and rumours of good results from tests of the controversial Busang gold samples being carried out in Australia at the moment. Golden Valley has an interest in the Muara Atan contract of work which contains part of the Busang deposit.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to four, while 38 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
In other local markets, futures related selling saw bond yields edge higher during the course of the morning as the market awaited Tuesday's "living wage" verdict by the AIRC.
By 12.50 p.m. (0250 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.86 percent, up from Friday's 7.82 percent.
The Australian dollar crept higher at the midsession as early support prompted scattered short-covering but shied away from testing US$0.7770 resistance.
By 12.50 p.m. (0250 GMT), the local dollar had drifted back up to US$0.7755/60 from an offshore low around US$0.7725 and up on Friday's late US$0.7750/55.
